title: Pan-Seared Ribeye Steak
summary: A pan-seared ribeye for one. It takes longer than fillet, even though it is cooked less, because of its size and the fat that has to render.

steps.text: Take the steak out of the fridge {timer:30} before cooking. Pat it completely dry with kitchen paper and season both sides generously with salt and pepper.
Heat a frying pan over a medium-high heat with a light coat of oil until very hot.
Lay the steak in the pan and do not move it. Sear the first side for {timer:3-4}, until a deep brown crust forms.
Turn the steak and sear the second side for {timer:3}.
In the last {timer:1-2}, add the butter to the pan, with the thyme, garlic and rosemary if using. Tilt the pan and baste the steak continuously with the foaming butter, using a spoon.
Move to a plate and rest for at least {timer:5} before cutting. The internal temperature should be {temp:52-55!} for medium-rare.

tips: Pat the steak completely dry before seasoning; moisture stops a good crust forming. Do not move the steak once it is in the pan. Basting with butter adds richness, and resting lets the juices redistribute. I love a large steak (300 g), but if you want to use smaller cuts, you can ask the AI assistant to adjust the cooking times.
